journal_lines: Roots in the water first, then down to the mud.
A frog on the root arch I was about to step over. Stepped around it.
The aerial roots hang like curtains. Patience required.
Dense, uneven wood. A life lived half in water.
The aerial root system extends twenty feet before the first trunk.
The tide came in while I was working. Adjusted.
The mangrove wood is dense and twisted with water history.
Crabs in the mud underneath the roots. One investigated a paw.
Working in standing water is slower and wetter.
The smell of salt and mud and organic rot. A particular kind of place.
Found the dry platform among the roots. Worked from there.
Mudskipper on the root I was using as a brace.
The fog came in with the tide. Worked by sound for a while.
A boat wedged in the roots. Old. Useful boards in it.
